title: A branch and its tips
hook: An evolutionary tree can show more than one ending.

knows: A family tree can split into branches.
doesNotKnow: Distinguish a species disappearing from extinction of its whole group.

misconception: The extinction of one species always ends the larger lineage.
objective: Distinguish a species disappearing from extinction of its whole group.

claims.text: An evolutionary tree can show more than one ending. In a toy dinosaur family tree, species A disappears while species B continues. What happens to the larger group containing both? In this constructed tree, one species ends while a second branch continues. The larger group remains represented through the continuing branch. One extinct member does not imply that every member of its group disappeared.
claims.source: Source lead to verify: OpenStax Biology 2e https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/20-1-organizing-life-on-earth. The illustrated A and B are hypothetical.

claims.text: Recall: In a model clade, one species disappears but another persists. Is the whole clade gone? A larger group can remain represented when at least one of its lineages persists.
claims.source: Source lead to verify: OpenStax Biology 2e https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/20-1-organizing-life-on-earth. The illustrated A and B are hypothetical.

recall.question: In a model clade, one species disappears but another persists. Is the whole clade gone?
options: Only if the extinct species returns
No; it remains represented by the survivor
Yes; one loss always ends a clade
recall.why: A larger group can remain represented when at least one of its lineages persists.
